classification_reasons: This round still carries a public-signature/contract decision (mean's parameter type, Collection[float]) taken in this design phase — sdlc.yaml's routine test excludes any contract change, so routine is unavailable regardless of blast radius or spec tightness.

Blast radius is small (only changes/0002-.../{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**}; no sample_pkg/*.py, tests/*.py or guardrail file touched this round; no sdlc.yaml risk_list item applies), but mean is brand-new code with zero existing test coverage (tests are written in phase c), so the 'code the existing tests already cover' leg of routine also fails.

Spec is now closer to tight — both Flagged concerns are decided and Requirements bullet 3 / the Design section's parameter-type paragraph correctly say so — but a symmetric staleness survives elsewhere in spec.md (see attempted/Spec-and-plan below), so 'no open concern' is true in substance (Flagged concerns section itself has no open item) but spec.md's prose is not perfectly self-consistent yet.
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's Proposed outcome, Constraints and Open questions against the current spec.md/plan.md/decisions-b.*. Nothing in this round changes the substance of the feature; it only reconciles documentation with decisions already taken. The substance (mean(values: Collection[float]) -> float, ValueError on empty input) still matches intent's Proposed outcome and both Open questions, now closed.

Spec and plan, point (a) proof: re-read evidence/claude-fix.json's 'result' field in full. It now narrates round 4's actual work ('applied the owner's overturn of Flagged concern 2 (Sequence[float] -> Collection[float]) to spec.md/plan.md, marked the panel ledger entry overturned, and added a test... Gate (b) result: parked (escalate)...') — this matches round 4's diff and round 4's actual outcome (an escalate on this reviewer's own stale-evidence finding), not the older 'iteration cap reached, no changes applied' story. The proof mismatch that drove the prior escalate is resolved: the committed run-log now accounts for the round it should describe. Cross-checked fix-response.md's explanation (claude-fix.json is written by the outer harness in a follow-up commit after a session ends, so it always lags one round behind the diff being judged inside a session, and commit 2e4ae9e — visible in git log — is exactly that catch-up commit) and found it internally consistent with what's on disk. Round 5's own claude-fix.json does not exist yet on this branch; per the same documented lag, that is expected (it will land after this session, in a later commit) and is not itself a red flag.

Spec and plan, point (b): compared the round's diff against the claim of what changed. spec.md's Requirements bullet 3 now states both Flagged concerns are decided (ValueError on empty input; Collection[float] parameter) instead of calling the parameter type open; the Design section's parameter-type paragraph now describes Collection[float] as decided ('decided in Flagged concerns, overturning this pass's original Sequence[float] framing') instead of an open Sequence-vs-Iterable question. Both edits match fix-response.md's description and close the specific inconsistency the prior escalate flagged as a nit.

Spec and plan, residual issue found: the Design section's separate Empty-input paragraph ('This is not settled here either (Flagged concerns)') was not touched this round and still contradicts Flagged concern 1, which shows 'decided (by panel): mean([]) raises ValueError(...)'. This is the same class of staleness as the concern-2 nit the prior round fixed, just for concern 1, and it predates this round (present since concern 1 was first decided by the panel, long before round 4). fix-response.md scopes this round's edit narrowly to 'Requirements bullet 3 and the Design section's parameter-type paragraph' only, so this gap is a known, not a newly introduced, omission. Judged this a nit under REVIEW.md ('style and naming are nits'; reserve Important for findings that break behavior, leak data or breach a policy): plan.md — the document phase c actually implements from — is fully consistent (signature, guard clause, four tests, Risks section all correctly state both concerns closed), so no implementer is misled by spec.md's residual prose gap. Not raised as an escalation reason, consistent with how the prior review treated the parallel concern-2 nit as 'not a reason on its own.'

Also noted, same family: the Flagged concerns section's two bullets each read as 'decided (...): <resolution> -- <original item text, still containing the word "undecided">' in one sentence, which looks self-contradictory on a literal read. This format is unchanged by this round and applies identically to both bullets (the never-escalated concern 1 and the previously-escalated concern 2), so it reads as a pre-existing template/authoring quirk rather than something this round should have caught or introduced. Nit, not a reason.

Proof (general): checked gate-b.json's embedded 'commands' check (build/test/lint output, head 312a101, round 4) against fix-response.md's round-5 claim of '5 passed... all green' — consistent (round 5 touches no source file, so the toolchain state is unchanged from round 4's recorded run; nothing to re-verify with new logs, and none of spec.md/plan.md/status.yaml changes would alter compileall/pytest/ruff behavior). claude-fix.stderr.txt/claude-b.stderr.txt contain only a boilerplate Claude Code trust-dialog warning, nothing that undermines the run's legitimacy.

Blast radius: confirmed via the diff's own diff --git headers that only changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**} are touched; grepped for sample_pkg/, tests/, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, sdlc.yaml as diff targets and found none; no sdlc.yaml risk_list item applies (no code exists yet to touch auth, data migrations, money movement or production config).

Policies: re-read decisions-b.json/decisions-b.md and the panel files for both concerns; the owner's overturn rationale for concern 2 (Collection[float] matches what sum/len actually need, at no extra cost, still rejects a generator) is faithfully carried into spec.md and plan.md; no policy skill (coding-standards, security-baseline, ux-conventions, data-conventions, definition-of-done) is silently skipped or contradicted by this round's prose-only edit.

Tests: no test code exists in this design-phase diff (correct — phase c writes it); plan.md's Proof section and spec.md's Acceptance section both consistently list the same four tests (normal, single-element, empty via ValueError, non-Sequence Collection via a set) and the same expected pass count (9); tests/test_flag.py and the existing five tests are untouched by this round.

status.yaml/gate-b.json/run-b.json: confirmed status.yaml's iterations_reset_by: luissiviero and iterations: 1 are consistent with one accepted round after the owner's sdlc:reset-iterations label; gate.result/reason still carry round 4's parked/escalate text (expected — the fresh gate check for this round runs after this review, not before).
